blocks.heading: Ownership sectors and organisation
blocks.text: Public and private sectors classify activity by ownership and control. A public-sector enterprise is owned and controlled by the state, whereas private-sector activity is owned and controlled by private individuals or organisations. A government-owned bus operator and an individually owned bus operator can provide the same service while belonging to different ownership sectors. Their activity does not settle their ownership. A mixed economy combines public and private activity. Public provision can pursue access to essential services or employment as well as financial sustainability. Private owners commonly seek profit and business survival, although a private organisation may also pursue social aims. Neither label proves that the organisation is efficient or that every service is free. Public enterprises may charge customers and private providers may supply services under government contracts. Organising privately can involve a sole trader, partnership or company; public activity can be organised through government departments or state-owned enterprises. Ownership forms are developed in topic 2.1. A company described as public limited has shares available to the public; that name does not by itself make it state owned. Ask who owns and controls it before assigning its ownership sector.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A municipal workshop, Ombili Services, is controlled by its local authority; nearby Ekuva Repairs is controlled by its individual owner. Both repair vehicles, but Ombili is public sector and Ekuva is private sector. Charging a repair fee does not change Ombili’s owner, and serving government vehicles does not make Ekuva a public enterprise.

blocks.heading: Public sector
blocks.text: The public sector comprises organisations owned and controlled by the state. State ownership, rather than whether the public uses a service, is the defining feature. Public provision may aim to extend access to essential services, while still needing to manage costs and finance its operations. A public enterprise may sell its output; charging customers does not turn state ownership into private ownership.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Assume the regional authority owns and controls Tano Passenger Services. Tano belongs to the public sector even when passengers pay fares. The fare is a source of revenue; the authority’s ownership is the classification test.

blocks.heading: Private sector
blocks.text: The private sector comprises activity owned and controlled by private individuals or organisations rather than the state. It includes individually owned businesses and companies, and can include organisations with social aims. Supplying a government customer does not by itself transfer ownership to government. A private company can grow very large while remaining private sector.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Amina owns Eteno Copy Shop and supplies printed worksheets to several state schools. The shop is private sector because Amina owns and controls it. The schools’ public status describes the customers, not the shop’s owner.
